meaning: Employ a tool, command, or feature for a purpose.
suggestions: Replace "utilize" with "use" when the meaning is unchanged.
note: Keep "utilization" when it names a measured capacity ratio.

meaning: Introduce the purpose of an action.
suggestions: Use "to" before the action unless the longer phrase prevents ambiguity.
note: Retain "in order to" when it clearly separates purpose from an infinitive complement.

meaning: Introduce the reason for a condition or result.
discouraged_forms: on account of the fact that
suggestions: Use "because" before a clause or "because of" before a noun phrase.
note: Use "due to" when it modifies a noun and remains the clearest option.

meaning: Refer to the present time.
discouraged_forms: at the present moment in time
suggestions: Use "now" for an immediate state or "currently" for an ongoing state.
note: Do not add a time marker when the tense already makes the timing clear.

meaning: State that a system or user has the capability to perform an action.
suggestions: Use "can" for ordinary capability statements.
note: Keep "is able to" when the distinction between inherent capability and temporary ability matters.

meaning: State a mandatory condition or action.
suggestions: Use "must" only when the statement is genuinely mandatory.
note: Preserve capitalized normative keywords such as MUST and MUST NOT in standards or contracts.

meaning: Place one event earlier than another.
discouraged_forms: in advance of the time when
suggestions: Use "before" for a direct time relationship.
note: Keep "prior" in established labels or when it modifies a noun, such as "prior version".

meaning: Place one event later than another.
suggestions: Use "after" and name the event that must finish first.
note: Keep "subsequent" when it distinguishes an item in an ordered legal or technical sequence.

meaning: Introduce a condition that controls an action or outcome.
suggestions: Use "if" for a positive condition or "unless" for a clear exception.
note: State the condition before the result when that order helps the reader act safely.

meaning: Introduce the subject of a statement.
discouraged_forms: in relation to the matter of
suggestions: Use "about" or rewrite the sentence so the subject becomes the direct object.
note: Keep a more specific relation word when it describes an actual dependency or comparison.

meaning: Check that a condition, value, or result is correct.
suggestions: Use the verb "verify" and name what the reader must check.
note: Use the noun "verification" when it names a formal phase, artifact, or test type.

meaning: Set options or values that control system behavior.
suggestions: Use "configure" followed by the component or setting.
note: Use "configuration" as a noun for the resulting set of values or a named configuration file.

meaning: Change an existing object, setting, or document.
suggestions: Use a direct verb such as "modify" and name the affected object.
note: Prefer a more precise verb such as "increase", "rename", or "replace" when it describes the change.

meaning: Choose an option after evaluating alternatives.
suggestions: Name the actor and use "decide" when the act of choosing matters.
note: Use "decision" when it names a stored result, approval record, or governance artifact.

meaning: State that a component or operation does not complete successfully.
suggestions: Use "fail" and identify the component or operation that fails.
note: Use "failure" as a noun when naming an event, state, category, or metric.

meaning: Cause a process, service, or procedure to begin.
suggestions: Use "start" followed by the process, service, or procedure.
note: Keep "initialize" when the action sets an object to its initial state rather than merely starting it.

meaning: Cause a process, service, or procedure to cease running.
discouraged_forms: cause the operation of to cease
suggestions: Use "stop" and name the process or service.
note: Keep "terminate", "cancel", or "shut down" when those actions have distinct technical effects.

meaning: Transfer a message, request, file, or value to a destination.
suggestions: Use "send" and identify both the data and its destination when useful.
note: Keep "transmit" when the physical or protocol-level transmission is the subject.

meaning: Provide a value or response to the caller.
discouraged_forms: give in return to the caller
suggestions: Use "return" without the redundant word "back".
note: Distinguish a returned value from a response sent asynchronously.

meaning: Make a new resource, file, account, or object.
suggestions: Use "create" and name the new object.
note: Keep "instantiate", "allocate", or "provision" when the implementation distinction matters.

meaning: Remove a resource or item so it is no longer available.
suggestions: Use "delete" and state whether recovery is possible when that affects safety.
note: Keep "remove", "revoke", or "detach" when the item continues to exist elsewhere.

meaning: Write current work or values so they remain available.
suggestions: Use "save" for the user action and identify the destination only when needed.
note: Use "persist", "commit", or "write" when those terms describe a distinct storage operation.

meaning: Choose a user-interface item without assuming a particular input device.
suggestions: Use "select" when keyboard, touch, and pointer input are all possible.
note: Use "click" when the physical pointer action itself is necessary to the procedure.

meaning: Provide text or a value in an input field.
suggestions: Use "enter" for data or "type" when the keyboard action matters.
note: Use "input" as a noun for data supplied to a system.

meaning: Make a file, page, menu, or application available for use.
suggestions: Use "open" and name the file, page, menu, or application.
note: Use "access" when permissions or availability, rather than a user-interface action, is the subject.

meaning: Dismiss a file, window, connection, or application.
suggestions: Use "close" for an object and "exit" for an application or mode when that distinction applies.
note: State whether unsaved work is lost when the action has that consequence.

meaning: Start an authenticated user session.
suggestions: Use "sign in" as the verb and reserve "sign-in" for a noun or adjective.
note: A project glossary may prefer "log in"; use one form consistently across the interface and documentation.

meaning: End an authenticated user session.
suggestions: Use "sign out" as the verb and reserve "sign-out" for a noun or adjective.
note: Match an established interface label when the product uses a different consistent term.

meaning: A value that uniquely names or distinguishes an entity within a scope.
suggestions: Use "identifier" unless the value is specifically numeric or an established field is named "ID".
note: Preserve exact schema, API, and interface field names.

meaning: Text that tells the user or operator that an error occurred.
suggestions: Use "error message" and describe its location separately when location matters.
note: Use "dialog", "banner", "notification", or "log entry" for a specific presentation format.

meaning: A message sent by a client to an API operation.
suggestions: Use "request" for the protocol message and identify the operation when needed.
note: Use "call" when referring to an SDK method call rather than the transmitted message.

meaning: A message that an API sends after processing a request.
suggestions: Use "response" for the protocol message and "return value" for a local function result.
note: Distinguish a synchronous response from a later callback, event, or notification.

meaning: A named input defined by an API operation, command, or function.
suggestions: Use "parameter" in prose and preserve abbreviated names only in code.
note: Use "argument" for a value supplied at a call site when that distinction matters.

meaning: A named element in a form, record, object, or message.
suggestions: Use "field" and identify the containing form, object, or message when needed.
note: Use "property", "column", or "control" when the data model defines that more specific term.

meaning: A network address at which an API operation is available.
suggestions: Use "endpoint" as one word and name the HTTP method separately when relevant.
note: Do not replace an exact product label, URI template, or schema field.

meaning: The process of verifying the identity of a user, service, or device.
suggestions: Use "authentication" in prose and explain the specific method when readers need it.
note: The abbreviation "auth" is acceptable in code, established product names, and tightly constrained tables.

meaning: The process of deciding which actions an authenticated identity may perform.
suggestions: Use "authorization" in US English and keep it distinct from authentication.
note: Preserve the spelling in code, protocol names, quotations, and products that use British English.

meaning: Secret or identifying data presented to authenticate an identity.
suggestions: Use "credentials" or name the exact item, such as a password, token, or certificate.
note: Do not imply that a public identifier is secret; describe each credential's handling requirements.

meaning: A recorded date and time associated with an event or value.
suggestions: Use "timestamp" and specify the format and time zone when readers must interpret it.
note: Use "date" or "time" alone when the value does not contain both components.

meaning: Attempt an operation again after it did not complete successfully.
suggestions: Use "retry" as a verb and state the limit or delay when it affects behavior.
note: Use "try again" when addressing a general audience and it reads more naturally in the interface.

meaning: A limit on how long a system waits for an operation.
suggestions: Use "timeout" as the noun and "time out" as the verb.
note: State the unit and whether the timer starts again after activity when that affects configuration.

meaning: A copy retained so data or a system can be recovered.
suggestions: Use "backup" as one word for the noun or adjective.
note: Describe retention, location, and recovery scope when those details matter.

meaning: Create a recoverable copy of data or a system.
suggestions: Use "back up" as two words for the verb.
note: Use "archive", "snapshot", or "replicate" when it names a technically different operation.

meaning: Restore a system or change to an earlier state.
suggestions: Use "roll back" as two words for the verb and "rollback" as the noun or adjective.
note: State the target version or state and any data-loss consequence.

meaning: Install and activate a software version in a target environment.
suggestions: Use "deploy" and name the version and environment when they are not already clear.
note: Keep "release", "publish", and "promote" when the delivery process gives them distinct meanings.

meaning: Stop and then start a process, service, or device.
suggestions: Use "restart" as one word and name the affected component.
note: Use "reboot" only when the operation specifically restarts an operating system or device.

meaning: A condition or task that must be complete before another task begins.
suggestions: Use "prerequisite" as one word in prose.
note: In a procedure, list concrete prerequisites instead of repeating that they are required.

meaning: Introduce an example that illustrates a statement.
suggestions: Use "for example" in running prose or "such as" before a short list.
note: The abbreviation "e.g." can be appropriate in tables, parenthetical notes, and space-constrained interfaces.

meaning: Temporary text or a value that another value will replace.
suggestions: Use "placeholder" and state the required replacement format when readers must supply a value.
note: Use "sample", "default", "sentinel", or "test value" when one of those distinct meanings applies.

meaning: Describe the leading member of a coordinated group without implying ownership.
suggestions: Use "primary" when it accurately describes the leading role in the system.
note: Preserve exact protocol terms, commands, branch names, and product identifiers; choose "controller", "source", or another precise term when roles differ.
